utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A very good morning to everyone. Let us hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, with Ruth Karper, for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. All fit and prepared for the hearing of today. I think we can start immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I spoke briefly to Ms. Tabeau this morning, Dr. Tabeau, and she explained to me that the Republic-wide figures broken down by ethnicity for the populations in Bosnia and Herzegovina are currently be reviewed in her office. The final figures in preparation of the report for the Krajisnik/Plavsic case which is due on the 30th of this month. It's her preference to provide us that report once it's completed, and since she is going to be testifying regarding the missing and dead in Prijedor, subsequently, she would prefer to testify regarding those figures once they are reviewed and finalised and put into a submitted report. Then also, both myself and Defence counsel would have the opportunity to review that report in its entirety prior to questioning her. But as Your Honours wish, she also informed that she did forget to bring the questionnaire but she has asked for it to be brought here, and it will be here by the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's better to rely on the updated figures. And if indeed, we could be in possession of this updated report before court recess, we have them all here on the 1st of August, it would be excellent and allow us to be prepared, also with a view that in fact as expected and requested by the Defence, you'll appear once again in this courtroom. I think it's a good solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I just go over the schedule for today briefly before the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There were some observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just in connection with the point that was raised, Your Honour, although my learned friend has limited his comments to the demographic figures of the population that are involved in Republika Srpska, if I may ask whether or not the preliminary results or the study that Dr. Tabeau has prepared for Bosnia-Herzegovina, commonly known as the federation, whether those figures are available today or, likewise, will we be provided with copies of that data later this month, before the commencement of the proceedings after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: My understanding, and the Doctor can correct me if I'm wrong, is that her report will include figures on -- she certainly has available figures on all of Bosnia-Herzegovina in both of the current entities. In fact, I think some of those figures -- I could be incorrect, on the Keraterm report, I think there's some reference to that. I think he raised a second point, but I forgot what it was. Obviously, the Doctor has knowledge of what the figures are, but it's just not finalised. If it's necessary to ask her questions about that today, she certainly can answer them, but she prefers to wait until all the figures are reviewed in her office and the report is in final form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed, it would be better to wait but, of course, to include the figures, not only for Republika Srpska but for the entire now state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I think we can proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know if Your Honours would like a brief preview of the day's events anticipated. But we do have a set of documents for distribution we've entitled List 6. It's about three centimetres' worth that I have in my hand here, and those are a review through all of the 19 binders we reviewed which documents have not yet come into -- been admitted in the trial that we think are highly relevant. That would be It's this list. It's hopefully, I believe, the last major set of documents that will be admitted or proffered. Secondly, Your Honour, yesterday Mr. President requested further information about how the -- I believe it's S221, the eight -- S220 to 2267, the eight pages of documents with signatures were actually obtained. And we checked yesterday with the person who actually made the physical arrest, took custody from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia from the accused, and that person is prepared to testify as to how he first obtained possession of those items, and he would be available after Dr. Tabeau. We have also distributed his notes today, this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Fast solutions are good solutions. We are looking forward to this. Thank you. I only may add, before we start, the further examination-in-chief, that it seems to be necessary, having had an overview. And additional thank you for the additional list, to that what you had cellophane. It may be necessary to read out in any event four of these documents during the next week. So I think everything is settled, and we can start, please. Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The only further direct examination would have been to the points regarding the total population changes in Bosnia-Herzegovina, so at this point I have completed my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I ask the Defence, then, to start the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Tabeau. My name is John Ostojic, and along with Branko Lukic, we represent Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a series of questions here today in connection with the area that you have a specialty, namely, scientific statistical demography. Bear with me, if you will, if at some time I misstate or will ask a question for purposes of definitional reasons, because I'd like to at least have a better understanding of both your report, the data provided, as well as the conclusions that you reached. Yesterday, on page 33, specifically line 23 in the transcript, you stated that your responsibilities while employed with the OTP, for the last two years or so, include "estimating demographic consequences of the conflict in the Former Yugoslavia, in particular, Bosnia and Herzegovina." My question to you is, when you used the "estimating," how would you define it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Estimating is producing measures, statistics, that describe the changes in the population, changes related to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So, in essence, you're providing us with statistics of the movement, if you will, of the population, and that is exactly what a demographer does. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is what, among other things, demographers do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In your process and deliberation of formulating your report, would it be fair to say that there's a two-tiered analysis?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could explain what you mean by a two-tiered analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try. I find the area somewhat interesting but complicated in many ways. The first tier, would you agree with me, would be the section that would be categorised as informational sources, and a demographer or a person such as a demographer, would take those informational sources and collect that. That would be one tier. The second tier would be taking those informational sources and making an application to those sources in order to reach your conclusions which would be called, I think, as you identify in your report, as the methodology.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this first section which you call informational sources, would you agree with me that that, in essence, is merely a collection of data that is not generated or produced by you but merely a collection of data from a third source?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that we understand each other --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Original sources are data collected by others. We process this information in the process of our project.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: These informational sources, just so that we again understand each other, are items such as, for example in this context and in your case, the 1991 census. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It also includes items such as the voter registration or the voters' register, as you refer to it in your report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now your report, having relied on these two informational sources, is as good or the quality of it is as strong as is the sources that you yourself relied upon in order to gather that data. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is -- the quality of sources, it is a precondition, a good quality of sources is a precondition of the outcome, a good outcome of the project.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if the sources, Dr. Tabeau are not as reliable, then ultimately, your report would also be considered less reliable. Correct? And less complete?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the quality of outcome depends on the quality of sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me switch for a moment, if I may, to the second tier of this two-tier analysis that generally is used by demographers, namely, the methodology. Is the methodology, in essence, the interpretation of those sources? Would that be a fair way to categorise and summarise that?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it includes interpretation of sources, but methodology is more than interpretation only. These are also tools that are used to reach our conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Within this second tier methodology, do you provide as a demographer any quality controls to secure that in fact that interpretation of the informational sources and data you are reviewing, whether or not quality controls for purposes of completeness and reliability are utilised

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quality controls, what do you mean by quality controls? When applying certain tools and reaching certain conclusions, we indeed do our best to ensure that the tools and the way they are applied are absolutely correct. And if -- I would think of quality controls in the context of this phase of our work, we indeed pay a lot of attention to quality control.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is the reason you pay a lot of attention to quality controls is because you want to ensure that the conclusions ultimately reached by a demographer are accurate and reliable?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So can you share with me, because I wasn't able to find it in your report, what quality controls did you utilise to ensure that both the two sources, two informational sources that you utilized, the 1991 census and the voter registration, were actually something that can be reliable and complete as it relates to demography?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quality controls in the sense -- I already said choosing tools that are appropriate and the way of application of the tools that is appropriate. This all has been done, and I believe you can easily see from the report what tools and how they have been applied. But I think that what you mean is rather quality control in the context of sources, so the choice of sources and completeness of sources, the reliability of sources. This is what you now mean by quality controls, I believe. Before I will answer how we approach these issues, I just want your confirmation that that is that type of quality controls you are asking me about right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In part, it is. I think there are -- you may agree with me that there's actually quality controls that relate to the informational sources that you as an independent and objective individual or expert in the field would look at and make an assessment of that, to determine whether it's even data that you should consider, and then ultimately the quality controls that should be in place to verify that indeed the conclusions reached based on both the methodology, which in your case I think you identified it as "linking," relating to those informational sources. So, in part, yes, but it's a two-fold question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I will first speak about sources. We certainly do a lot of quality controls with sources. It is -- before we can even start our analysis, we must complete a lengthy process of data preparation. So it is not that we, having received a source, can immediately start our analysis. We check, always check, the completeness of the source. We always check the frequency distributions of the variables. We work with individual data so it is necessary to look for outliners, to explain what are the reasons that certain outliners are seen in our frequency distributions. We compare the sources that we received with additional information, auxiliary information, and based on this, we draw conclusions about to what extent our sources are complete and reliable. With the population census, the task is rather easy because there are official publications of census figures, and we can compare results of our queries with the official publications. The situation is different with the voters register. Population census is just a standard source of information used in producing demographic statistics and socioeconomic statistics related to the population. Voters' register is a different type of source. We don't use these type of sources in producing official statistics. Still, I believe this is a reliable and large source, exhaustive, relatively exhaustive, that can be used to draw conclusions about the population and its composition. Again, we work, once we have original data in our office, we start data processing by doing the same things, comparing the size of this collection with other sources about the population, if there are any existing, of course, to compare. We check distributions of items included in that database. We look for outliners. We correct mistakes that we see in the databases. So there is a lot of quality controls. Of course, we could write a hundred -- hundreds of pages about how we do it and what are the results of this process, but I believe no one in this court would be able to go through these pages. It is just part of our work. And regarding the matching, we indeed should have included summary information about the quality of matching by criteria used, percentage of matches obtained. And if necessary, I can prepare this type of overview.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get back to that in a moment, but thank you for that offer. With respect to voter registration and the voters' registry that you reviewed, you yourself consider that to be a not -- not an official data source that demographers use for producing official statistics. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just want to confirm it. If you take the fact that you have two informational sources, namely, the census of 1991 and the voter register, or the voters' register as you referred to it in your report, and if one is not as -- is not official, would that allow us to opine and conclude that it is less reliable than the census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, reliability and being official are two different things. Well, official statistics are produced by statistical authorities in all countries in order to be used by -- consistently used by the society. These are just reference figures that we all need. Unofficial figures are produced by other organs than official statistics, official statistical office, but it doesn't mean that these figures are unreliable or not useful. There are many surveys in every country - I'm speaking about western, at least, countries - that are widely used and are never called official. So this is the same situation we are dealing here with the voters' register. It is not used for producing official statistics but it is a large source of information about the population, about the size of the population, its structure. And I believe it can be -- this is just a survey. It can be used as a survey of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, Dr. Tabeau, that in fact the voters' registry does not include something that seems to be referenced and in fact something that was asked of you to do, and that is to determine the ethnic population of a certain area in Bosnia and Herzegovina. You would never or rarely, in any country or state, find that there's an ethnic composition or ethnic reclassification of people within documents known as the voters registry. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct when saying that there is no item "ethnicity" included in the voters register. This is very correct. This information is not there, not in this collection. But by matching sources, linking records from different sources, we increase our information about individuals. And after having linked records from the voters' register backwards to the census, we are able to include the ethnicity reported in the census for every voter that had been matched with the census. And this practice is a standard procedure used in demography.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Doctor, if you know, what are the generally or widely accepted or understood flaws and inaccuracies upon relying on voters registers in coming up with statistical information in connection with demography? What are those flaws, do you know?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the voters' register as such as a source?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I think we must mention that the source is incomplete in the sense that certain age groups of the population are not there. These are those who are not eligible to vote, the population, from birth up to the age of 17. Secondly, voters' register is -- only includes information about voters who registered to vote. Registration is not obligatory. So those who want to register, register. Who didn't want, didn't go, for any reason, are not there. So the source is large, but incomplete, right. So two basic flaws I can mention immediately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree with you. I categorise them as voter apathy, or apathy, as one, and age elimination because we reduce and do not include a certain segment of the population that is alive, may be living in the area and may be of one or the other ethnic composition that we're discussing here today. Can you provide with me, please, what the percentages are for both, within that voters registry, of what that apathy was and what that percentage was of age elimination?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You, of course, know that I can not because, in order to do so, I would need information about the population at that time, which I could compare with the voters' register. And I have used voters's register because there is no information about population at that time in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We haven't had census, population census, in Bosnia since 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forgive me, Dr. Tabeau, I'm not sure if we understand each other. At the moment I'm not talking about the census. I'm talking about voter registration. You are familiar that in 1991 or 1992, there was actually an election in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Correct? And we can assume from that there were actually data and statistics available which would provide us with, at the very least, the voters registry?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that to answer specifically your question, I would need to compare the population in the voters' register with the actual population at that time. And I don't have this population. I am repeating what I already said. I don't think that this type of comparison you are suggesting is the way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Would you think that, in order to verify the accuracy and reliability of one of the informational sources such as voters' registry, that one would want to obtain that information both for completeness and thoroughness of your report? Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are ways to assess completeness of this source and reliability of this source as well. But in order to do so, resources, extra resources, would be needed to run a survey in a certain area and to compare the population and the voters' register. But I want to note that we are speaking about demographic changes in a population that was in a conflict period long time. And in this period, in such periods, it is unjustified to expect that there are sources about this population related to the population size and other aspects of the population as in normal times. So the situation is just abnormal. I would put it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, Doctor, did you even try to obtain the 1990 voter register from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, you mean? 1990, I think that I have that census, the 1991 census.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know. And I may be speaking a little too fast, and I apologise. I'm still on voters' registry, so I could understand it. And I don't understand it, obviously, as clearly as you do. But did you, in order to ensure that relying upon the voters' registry as you did for 1997, did you try and seek to obtain documents similar to those that existed as a result of the 1990 election in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. This is the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, could you please take care not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the same time, I believe that the 1997 election and the 1990 election you mentioned are not the same elections. But participation rate can be quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Shouldn't we, before we conclude something like that, obtain the information and then develop a methodology like you developed such as linking or matching before we can actually leap to that conclusion? Wouldn't that be a better way to do it?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would love that. If you give me money and people, we will do that. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have been asking for that for many years now, both money and friends. Anyway, if I can switch the topic, I apologise, with respect to the voter registry, or one last question in connection with that, I hope: Do you know what the percentage of the population actually voted in 1997?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: OSCE made some estimates and they vary depending on the municipality. But we can conclude that approximately, say, 75 per cent, up to 80 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's for the entirety of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the country as such, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me what the word "margin of error" means?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Margin of error.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an acceptable error one makes presenting estimates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that demographers and scientists such as yourself, Dr. Tabeau, in preparing these types of demographic studies, that in fact margins of error is something that you would include in every report so that the reader and the person who is digesting that information can conclude whether or not your report is objective and sound? Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what your margin of error was with respect to both the informational sources that you rely upon in order to reach your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the margin of error should be seen in the context of particular estimates, statistics, that we present in our report and not in the context of sources. And indeed, certain fractions of ethnic composition should be additionally shown together with -- within confidence intervals, within a range of possible error. I would put it this way. We haven't done this in this report. But you should also remember that this is a report, one of our first reports, and we have been doing -- improving, say, ourselves, and now we are presenting more recent reports, these type of statistics as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are both margin of errors and confidence levels one and the same or are they two distinct areas that a demographer and a scientist such as yourself would utilise in a report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, confidence level is actually a way of expressing -- expressing uncertainty related to a particular measure presented in a study. Confidence and error are two related things. Confidence, an area, say, not a point estimate but an area within which the estimate is likely to be contained, are basically the same. It is the way of speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I again just to repeat, if I may, and I apologise if you've answered this question already, in your report we see no estimates or no conclusions with respect to what the margin of error is, and we also do not see any -- I got it. I'm just waiting for them to catch up this one time. Any confidence levels that may or may not have been utilized by you or your staff in reaching your conclusions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is not, correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may turn briefly to the census, the informational source that we've identified as the census, which is the 1991 census that you gleaned or that you reviewed, with respect to that census or the second informational source, before you make any conclusions, do you do any study or evaluation to determine whether or not that informational source is reliable and is something that you would utilise in your application and, ultimately, your conclusion in reaching your findings?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a very general question. If you could be more specific, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. Did you examine whether or not in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in 1991, whether there were any census controls that were put into place?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about these statistical authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I believe there were no such activities like cleaning the census. And this was related to the conflict that started shortly after the census was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that without these census controls, the 1991 census would be deemed less reliable than if those controls would have been put in place?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, always after cleaning, data collection is of better quality than without. But at the same time, I believe that even though we realise there are certain errors in the census, it is not that all the data is wrong and cannot be used. It is absolutely not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that it is, Doctor. Can you point to me where you in your objective report identify for us that the 1991 census that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French English transcripts you're relying upon as an informational source is either, in some part or to a certain degree, erroneous, flawed, or inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we tried to say something about the quality of the census. But indeed, the section is brief in this report. The only problem we mentioned is misspelled names. That it is a problem, a major problem, I would believe, from the point of view matching sources. And we have spent a lot of time on correcting the names and certain procedures were applied to eliminate errors from the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Before we get into the actual errors within the names, what my concern initially and what my question in part was, the census controls that were missing in Bosnia-Herzegovina, so that I may have a better understanding, would they be things that would include like a pilot survey or a sample survey, which are two distinct things, though, correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, usually, before the census starts, there is a pilot or -- pilot census, microcensus, in which the questionnaire is tested and possible mistakes are detected and conclusions from this pilot are used in this census itself. As far as I know, there was no pilot or additional surveys.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me understand that. If you as a scientist will take a data such as the informational source, the 1991 census, would it be fair to say that your first step is to determine how accurate and how reliable that informational source is. So you would, in essence, proceed and ask someone or try to determine whether in fact there was a pilot survey done which, as you said, is a microcensus, pre-census. It is a study that is done before in order to make verification and accuracy of the upcoming census. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my answer is different in this case. It is -- again, I must stress that we deal here with a very extraordinary situation. We are supposed to estimate demographic consequences of certain situation to the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And we actually have difficulties with finding sources. So the choice is either we can use the sources that exist in the best possible way or not to do anything. I believe that even though there was no pilot or pre-census, and even though the statistical authorities in the country in Bosnia and Herzegovina haven't done much to improve the quality of the source, we have done a lot to improve the quality of the source here in our office. And let me finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know a lot about problems related to the census. But still, I think, it is not -- the problem is very complex. I wouldn't even expect that statistical authorities at that time, in 1991, in Bosnia, were able, had necessary equipment, software, to do this type of procedures that we are able to do today. So it is -- I don't think that certain things were possible at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, Doctor, at any time make any effort whatsoever to determine whether or not there was a pilot survey done in Bosnia and Herzegovina in connection with the upcoming 1991 census? I understand your conclusion, but did you verify the fact that it was not done or did you simply reach that conclusion as a matter of convenience?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had several meetings with the statistical authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina at which I discussed, among other things, the census. And never any one of the people of statistical authorities has mentioned this type of survey to me. So this is the basis on which I draw this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. That's the pilot survey. Did you determine whether or not a sample survey, which is a survey that's done, in essence, after the census for purposes of verification of the reliability and completeness of the data provided? Did you determine whether or not the representatives in Bosnia-Herzegovina ever conducted a sample survey?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I already said previously, I concluded that there was no such a survey.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with me generally the difference between what a raw count is in a census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Raw count, you mean just the count of certain -- I don't know, categories you are interested in as obtained just from the raw data, from not clean data.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that a raw count is more reliable than a census would be in any situation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I am confused because my understanding of raw count is different than your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's go with your understanding. How did you understand the raw count?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Raw count is just a number, absolute number, of certain individuals reported in a source like a census.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You don't find that a raw count or an actual head count is more reliable and more thorough than a census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that -- I'm still confused a little bit. But a raw count is probably, for you, an estimate not based on the census but on other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, a raw count to me, Doctor, is the actual count of the specific number of people that may reside in a certain geographical area, whereas a census, with its inherent inconsistencies and inaccuracies, doesn't come -- as you know from the literature, doesn't even come remotely close to a raw count in terms of both its reliability and completeness. Wouldn't that be true?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are speaking about the population, the actual population, the number of the actual population as it is in reality, and the estimate of this population obtained from the census, I believe. So the raw count is the true size of this population for you, I believe. Well, there is something like this, the true size, the true number, but how can you obtain the true number otherwise then by using a source like survey? So you must also accept that we obtain information about population from certain surveys. Always any aggregate statistics are based on the individual data collected in a survey, like the population census. And in every survey, there are errors.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And my question to you is with respect to the informational source that you've identified as the 1991 census. What, in your opinion, based upon a reasonable degree of scientific certainty, is the margin of error?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to answer this question. No one is, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your field of study and practice is actually making estimates from the data and information that you would gather and glean. Can you, in the field of specialty in which you received a Ph.D., provide us with an estimate of what that margin of error is, an approximation, if you will?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, but the question, I think -- excuse me. It's not clear what counsel is referring to, the margin of error for what specific figure? I don't think it's possible to give a confidence level margin of error without giving a specific statistic, asking about a specific statistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the question of Defence counsel is, to a certain extent, fair and relevant and it would be indeed relevant to hear what based on your experience in all other countries, in a kind of worst-case scenario, the margin of error can amount to and translate this to the area and the environment in Bosnia-Herzegovina, with all the potential mistakes made when coming to these figures in the census. My understanding of this margin of error is to point out in both directions what would be the worst-case scenario. Is it possible, from your general point of view, to say plus, minus 10 per cent? This would amount to worst-case. Is it possible and is it, on a scientific basis, possible to come to this margin of error in general, not related to Bosnia-Herzegovina, first of all, and then probably come closer to that what we have before us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I believe the question is still related to this error between the true population size of the actual population and the estimated population size as based on the population census. And, of course, I am absolutely unable to indicate a number that would be an approximation of such an error. I can only say that the number of individuals reported in the population census in 1991, 4.4 million, approximately, individuals is, in my view, an overestimation, I believe a slight overestimation, because I believe, first of all, it is -- the concept of the population is not clear. It's not clearly defined in the documents I know from the statistical authorities. We don't know exactly whether the statistics they present based on the census refer to the de facto population or the de jure population. De facto is the actual population living in the area. De jure is the population that lives there actually, plus those who are registered in the population register. So it is slightly unclear. This is one thing. And another thing, there are duplicates in that census. Many people, I think several thousand people, were reported twice, or even more times sometimes. And this is related to the fact that household head who was interviewed often reported children, for instance, students studying in a different place and these students were also interviewed by other interviewers and were included as individuals in statistics. So these are the duplicates. When we assume that the population reported includes these duplicates and also population that is absent de facto in the country but working, say, overseas, then these are the two reasons for the overestimation of the population size. How large it is, it is difficult to say for me right now. But I believe that statistical authorities have not made clear indications about how they deal with these issues when presenting their official statistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. Defence may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me, if I may, examine the actual census that was taken in 1991 but more from a -- help me understand how the census was taken. Censuses can be taken, and are taken, in various countries in different forms. They sometimes send the census information or packet to the individual households and expect the individual citizens to return those forms back to the bureau of census. Correct? That's one way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in this instance in Bosnia-Herzegovina, actually the way it was done is that the offices, the federal offices in Bosnia-Herzegovina, hired and employed individuals to go out and actually, on foot, take this questionnaire house to house. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you know what the reliability or, statistically, would you know how many of those reports came back either not filled completely or having a result where the household members were not found?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many households were not found. This type of information is unavailable to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have information which would let us know whether or not each of the data information requested in the census questionnaire, whether or not any of those were omitted or not filled in by the various citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you mean incompleteness of the responses?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that I don't possess this information, but we learn from the data itself about the incompleteness of responses. It is very easy to check how many responses were wrong or incomplete, missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Isn't that important if --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varies depending on the item, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Isn't that statistical figure important, at the very least, if you're going to make any reliance upon the informational source of the 1991 census, namely, that if 25 per cent, hypothetically, 25 per cent of the respondents to the questionnaire or interview in 1991, failed or refused to identify both their income and/or their educational background, wouldn't that be significant in determining whether or not relying on such data is reasonable?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it is completely irrelevant to this report because the information I used is just the individuals, counts of individuals. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- you are probably thinking about the second part of the report, where the socioeconomic characteristics were discussed. But we are not discussing this today, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So table 4, for example, which discusses the educational part, that's not something that I understand you discuss and that's not something that we are prepared to discuss today. Would that be a fair summation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can answer your question by showing you the number of missing responses on this particular item from the census later, if it is -- if you -- I think I believe it is such a basic information that we can provide it very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the statistical process called imputation?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? These are only words. Please explain because our understanding can be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that. Do you as a demographer, have you ever heard as a scientist, a statistical demographer, ever heard of the word "imputations"?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said quote - I don't see it in the transcript -- quote imputation or -- ?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I was merely putting emphasis and underscoring the word "imputation".

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard it in many different context, but I need to know more specifically what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure. Maybe you'll like my definition. It's my understanding that an imputation, in fact, in statistical demographic, scientific statistical demography, is in essence where, if you take an informational source such as a census, that the people at the census bureau take what's called this imputation and fill in the gaps where the individuals did not provide answers. That's what an imputation is, isn't it, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the meanings is this, but I wouldn't expect that anyone imputed any information because the questionnaires were scanned. And this is how we obtain the data. So it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe I don't understand you. I'm not suggesting that you or your office would impute that information. I'm talking about, in 1991, the people who were conducting the census. I'm confident that they were familiar with the statistical process called imputation.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interviewers, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. The actual authorities who gathered the data and who actually ultimately created the report that became the 1991 census, do you know and did you at any time ask any of the authorities that you've met with whether or not they considered imputations and to what extent were imputations applied in the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't discuss the issue of imputation with the local authorities in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In order to be able to rely on an informational source, the more verification as to its credibility and reliability that we can do would give us a higher confidence level, would it not, than in fact that data that we're ultimately relying on to prepare conclusions, whether it be for an independent company or a court would be necessary? Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it would be indeed beneficial to have an opinion of an outside body on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm merely slowing down, Doctor, just so that -- unfortunately, I was speaking far too fast. I want to have a better understanding of this issue and area, so bear with me if I pause either mid-sentence or after your answer for any length of time. Merely I'm just trying to allow everyone to catch up and to digest some of the answers that are being provided. On page 56, Doctor, of yesterday's testimony, you answered a question by my learned friend that since the report that you provided to the Court that we have before us, since that time, you have acquired "new sources, extensive sources." I'm sorry, page 37. It was day 56. I misspoke. Page 37, lines 8 through 11, if I may. Since that report, you acquired "new sources, extensive sources, and received, for instance, a more recent version of the list of missing persons, so the sources that we have now at our disposal are much more extensive and much more reliable." Do you remember giving that testimony yesterday, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to conclude or would it be unfair to say that the sources that were relied upon in preparing and ultimately reaching the conclusions identified in your report were far less extensive and far less reliable than those that you have in your possession today?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May I object for a moment. I believe, and perhaps the Doctor could answer, but I believe it's taken out of context, in that the doctor was answering at that time information regarding missing and killed, while she is testifying at the moment regarding population changes. Obviously, the list of missing persons does not relate to the census but to the persons who are missing or killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's very fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, in that context, though, would you agree with me that you have obtained other informational sources, not just for the missing and the dead, but other informational sources that are much more extensive and much more reliable than those utilised in the report that you prepared and submitted to us, namely, dated April 19th, 2001?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you think of sources about the population, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Have you since 1991 tried to obtain any such information that would verify some of the conclusions or the data that are provided by the 1991 census or the voters' registry?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- well, regarding the population as a whole, it is impossible to find a source that would cover the whole population in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So the census, the 1991 census, is the last latest complete source of information about the population. Regarding the voters' register, we indeed completed -- obtained additional information. We possess now the voters register 2000 that has been compared to the voters' register 1997, 1998. And the conclusion is that the overlap between the voters' registers are very, very large. So the population reported in the voters' register or registers, say better, is largely the same in all voters' registers that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are we able, Doctor, from your report, in any fashion whatsoever, determine what the movement of population was in Bosnia and Herzegovina, specifically in Prijedor; are we able to determine or even glean from that report what that movement was from April 1992 through September 1992, which is a period of specific interest to us all?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The movement, population movement discussed in my report are actually shown at the moment of the election in 1997. So we are unable to say anything about this particular period.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in fact, all the data that's provided and all the conclusions that you reached is for information as it looked if you were to freeze-frame that time as it looked in 1997. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that the conclusions reached and the data provided by you has nothing to do, and we cannot at any point, based upon a reasonable degree of scientific demography, determine what that movement of population was from January 1992 to, let's say, January 1993?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are unable to specifically explain or show, describe, the movements in this period but we believe, and I think not only us but also other organisations, that what we saw in 1997 is largely the consequence of what was happening in 1992, including the period you mentioned. And there were only a few returns between, say, the end of the conflict, end of 1995, and 1997, of the population who used to live in these areas, including Prijedor. So those who left these areas during the conflict largely lived at new locations by 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested as much in 1995 as I am in 1992. Are we able to discern from any of the data that you provide whether or not there was a movement of population and what specifically that movement of population was from April through December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't provide this information in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mention on page 38 of yesterday's transcript or testimony, during direct examination on page 15, that there are international guidelines regarding the way the census should be conducted. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I understand that you have been busy the last couple weeks. Actually, you testified in two other cases or three other cases?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Some other cases. Fair enough. Approximately, or exactly two weeks ago, on July 10th -- actually, two weeks and one day, July 10th, 2002, you were asked about certain international recognised standards for the -- for a census. And specifically, Madam, if you can reconcile this for me, Dr. Tabeau. On page 10809 of the July 10th, 2002 transcript, you were asked a question as follows, on line 12: "Are there internationally accepted guidelines for the conduct of censuses in countries? Can you please comment on that." Question, again on line 24: "So do we have certain international recognised standards? " Answer by you, Dr. Tabeau, on line 25 of that same page 10809, as follows: "Well, I must say I don't know. I may expect there are such guidelines, but as far as I know, every country is free as to how to apply, induce, these guidelines." Just for the record, it continues on page 10810 of that July 10th, 2002 transcript. Did you learn what those international guidelines were since two weeks ago, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I checked whether such guidelines are produced and who does it. It is indeed United Nations and statistical authorities, Statistics Division of the Department of Economic and Social Affairs in New York.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that in 2001, April 19th, which is the date of your report, despite the fact that you were on the team that was evaluating these informational sources and reaching the various conclusions, you hadn't, until two weeks ago, known that there were even international guidelines that would applicable for conducting censuses in countries? Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't sure, so the answer "I didn't know" actually is correct in this case. As I said, I may expect -- I might expect there were such guidelines. Moreover, you forgot that this report was written together with Helge Brunborg, who is an employee of Statistics Norway, and actually he is an expert regarding this type of issues. So I relied in this case on his expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Of this report, with the three individuals that are named on it, what portion of it did you specifically do, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular report, we completed the analysis of population movements based on the two sources, census and voters' register. This is the results that are shown in figure, I believe, 3. And next one, figure 4, and the mapping. And the second part of the report, socioeconomic characteristics of persons missing and dead. You should also remember that this is a project in which very many people are involved, and certain things had been done in the beginning of this project by other people. And the part related to the censuses was done by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you also the individual who prepared and performed most of the data that's provided on table 4 of your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did this part of the analysis, the parts I mentioned, together with Torkild Lyngstad.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that very shortly, I hope. Let me finish very briefly with respect to the census. Based on your experience as you told us yesterday, specifically on page 38, line 20, you identified the fact that: "I myself participated as an interviewer during my university education in one of the population censuses in Poland." And that appears on page 38, lines 20 through 22, of yesterday's transcript. Reconcile this for me, if you will, Doctor, please: When asked on July 10th, 2002, whether you had any involvement in conducting or participating in censuses, you responded on page 10811, line 3 -- let me read the question: "I understand, thank you. Another question which follows after your submission, from your professional background, in fact, I see that you are dealing mostly with mortality. Is that correct?" Answer: "Yes, that is correct." Question: "Not with the demographic issue and statistics?" Answer: "Very much." Question: "Not, census to be honest?" Answer: "Not census as much. I was never involved in conducting censuses." On line 10, again, page 10811 in the transcript of July 10th, 2002. My question to you: Which is it, Dr. Tabeau? Were you involved in a census as you told us yesterday, or were you not and you were never involved in a census, as you told the Court under oath on July 10th, 2002?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I was telling the truth in the other testimony and also yesterday here in this courtroom. I was asked then at that time in the other testimony about my professional qualifications. As a professional, I have never been involved in conducting census. And this is perfectly true. I was involved in a census as a census interviewer during my university education as a young student. I was a student of the first year then. I would not consider that professional experience that can be reported here in this Court to prove that I have qualifications as a census expert. Definitely, this is not experience that can be seen in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, with all due respect, that's why I'm just asking you to reconcile that issue for me. And thank you very much for that. In your experience as a census interviewer, whether it was during your university or college days or during your review of such data, did you ever come to a situation where you found that the people who were providing the information were inflating or exaggerating items that are provided or asked for by the census, such as income or education?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly, I cannot recall any experience with this type of issues from the time I was interviewing people. I cannot say that from my own experience I know the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But the literature is actually quite extensive when it discusses that one of the flaws or inaccuracies with the census, whether it be done by an individual interviewer or mailed out to various households, they find that those inaccuracies stem in part, and in essence, from both exaggerated and inflated data that would be provided by the individuals. Correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French English transcripts

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there is a lot of literature that is related to this type of issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Based upon a reasonable degree of scientific certainty, what is the margin of error with respect to this very issue that you feel is appropriate for the 1991 census in which you rely upon?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you expect me to mention a number, the size of the error, acceptable error. I, again, cannot say right now what would be such an error. But in statistics generally, in mathematical statistics, 5 per cent error when providing an estimate is an acceptable error.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there, Doctor, any verification done to determine whether the data that was provided by the citizens in Bosnia and Herzegovina from a secondary source, whether there was any work performed to make verification -- you know what? I should repeat that question. I apologise. Can I strike that and start over?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I briefly interrupt you. We have really to concentrate on the relevant issues. The relevant issues - we just conferred - in this case seem not to be education or income; it's a question of people living in the area, of missing people, people being maybe deported from one area to the other. But we shouldn't go into details of these additional questions of the demographic science.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, may I briefly respond to that, if I may? Your Honour, in the fourth amended revised indictment, as well as during the opening statement by the Office of the Prosecutor and throughout their case in chief in this case, the Prosecution has alleged that a various group, namely intellectuals and those who were better educated than the actual norm of society, were specifically being targeted by various members or groups in Prijedor specifically. It is that allegation, Your Honour, that I think that they have consistently made, and therefore have asked, I believe, Dr. Tabeau and other scientific demographers, to conclude for the Court data which we completely disagree with and dispute. And the reason comes because as an issue that is part and parcel with, as I believe the doctor will agree with me, the level of education that perhaps individuals may have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Respectfully, we don't need any kind of science to know that there isn't such a link in general between education and the income, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, just briefly if I may, with the Court's permission, ask one further question: When you take an informational source and you look to determine or verify the accuracy of that, would it be fair to say that scientists and demographers such as yourself, in order to make that verification, would consider what's identified and called as a secondary source?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And for example, if we were to study or make any observations with respect to education, the data provided to us that you relied upon is this 1991 census. In order to determine both reliability, completeness, and thoroughness, one would from a secondary source obtain the data and information from places like the university, the college, the postgraduate schools that are in the area that you're studying. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is all correct. It is, again, a matter of time and resources needed to collect this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you or did your group and department, did you at any time, in an attempt to determine the reliability and completeness of your findings, did you seek out these secondary sources such as universities to determine whether or not the accuracy of the data provided in the 1991 census would be considered reliable?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. It was absolutely impossible for me within these two years to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We spoke briefly of the reliability of various sources and documents. Are you familiar with the widely accepted factors that may affect accuracy and reliability such as synthetic errors, balancing errors, late adds, and whole person imputations? Are you familiar with those terms?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they are not terms -- again, you would need to explain exactly what you mean, but I am familiar with these types of terms. What is your understanding of these types of terms, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In your report, do you at any time factor in these widely accepted factors in order to let us know how accurate or how reliable the conclusions or the bases of the documents you relied upon are by utilising any one or a number of these factors?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are again speaking about the second part of the report in which we study socioeconomic characteristics of persons missing and dead. And in this context, I must say I did not present any measures of accuracy, completeness, and reliability of the information analysed in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's then go quickly, if we may, to the missing and the dead, as we've identified them, if I may. And that's the report that was discussed. The data that we have before us, as you stated on page 37 with respect to that, would be considered less, respectfully, extensive and less reliable than the data that you have in your possession since this report 19th of April, 2001. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what is the actual question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought -- I'll restate it.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very long question, so I missed the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know. That happens a lot. I'm sorry. My question to you, Doctor, is this: In light of the fact that you stated yesterday that you have available and in your possession more extensive data or data which is more extensive or much more reliable, is it fair to conclude that the material in connection with specifically the missing and dead that we discussed here yesterday and today, in part, that it would better to rely and wait to get that complete report before we actually go through each of the tables that were discussed here?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, then: Did you at any time or did your office at any time consider with respect to quality control items, since we're talking about dead and missing people, similar to those secondary sources such as the universities that we've mentioned, did you consider as a quality control reviewing or analysing any such secondary sources to determine the number of missing or dead persons in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, the premise of the question that we're discussing, the missing and dead, I thought was absolutely inaccurate. We choose on direct examination not to do that because the doctor is preparing a report with better and updated sources. I thought counsel was going to cross-examine on the new report once it's done. I don't think there should be two cross-examinations on that, so I'd ask that he choose whether to cross-examine once the report is completed or do it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's always --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed, we should wait for the second report, no anticipated cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may continue, Your Honour, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar, Doctor, with the methods used to compare the accuracy of data that's provided such as models known as the total error model and the lost function analysis?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must say that these are tools that I certainly heard of, but I believe that it is a little bit unfair to ask me questions about any method that can be applied to do with this type of operation. I would rather prefer to speak about the methods I will present you in my report, and then we can discuss to what extent these are appropriate tools.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: As always, I cannot -- I'm just a human being and don't know everything and anything. And I am -- what I have done, I understand how I did it and why I did it, and please ask me about these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fair, Doctor. Thank you very much. Just a couple other questions. In your report, if you can tell us whether or not in determining the movement of population in Bosnia and Herzegovina, specifically in Prijedor, did you or your office at any time take into consideration the voluntary movement of the Muslim population in April and May of 1992, specifically, the approximate 15.000 to 20.000 people that evacuated the area at the commencement of the war on April of 1992 in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking this generally, in my work generally, or in the context of this report? In both cases, I must say I don't possess any information, specific information, in terms of figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to state that if that information is available and produced to you, it may, in fact, alter dramatically the conclusions that are reached within your report?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report for Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question right now. I would have to see the figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just a few more questions, if allowed. With respect to the methodology that was used in conducting your report, namely, this matching or linking as you've described it, can you tell us what the widely accepted or what the literature says is actually the flaws and/or inaccuracies of utilising only one source for purposes of both matching and linking? That was the end of the question.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are speaking about matching or linking, speaking about one and the same thing, and this is always done in the context of more sources, more than one. So there must be at least two sources to be matched with each other. And when matching sources, we must think of having at our disposal a characteristic of individuals in both sources that can be easily compared and specifically compared, that this characteristic would allow us to decide that these particular records, two records, are the same in both sources. If there is no such characteristic, the matching becomes more complex and problematic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And problematic in the sense that it becomes more flawed and more inaccurate, correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's why scientists such as yourself and people who are in the field of demographics actually, in order to determine or to reach an acceptable, reliable, and complete conclusion of the report, seek out not only secondary sources but also obtain for this methodology of linking and matching, they would make comparative analysis to more than just one-on-one sourcing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that I should explain a little bit more about matching. So matching, once it is done with the census, it is done between all sources. So it is not that we match only two sources. At the time, we match two sources, but once all sources are matched with the census, the sources are matched also with each other. So in this way, we compare individually very many sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. Your Honour, it may be an appropriate time to take a break. I truly only have approximately 10 or 15 minutes left. However, if I can be given the questionnaire, I would be able to at least conclude that so we don't have to come back to it later. And it may be longer just based on the questionnaire, if permitted. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope during the break the Defence can be provided with the questionnaire. And as usual, the same request by the Bench, to be informed. And I want to recall before going to the break that we still expect the response from the side of the Defence as regards the fourth notice of the OTP as regards 92 bis statements. We have already the answer to the fifth, but not the fourth. If we can do this after the break. Thank you. The trial stays adjourned until 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Doctor, just briefly to conclude the area that we were discussing, in discussing the secondary sources which may be utilised by scientists and demographers such as yourself, secondary sources such as the administrative records of births, deaths, legal immigration and legal emigration. Are usually considered by persons in your profession in analysing and computing data in reaching your conclusions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In this report dated April 2001, had you, Doctor, ever used or examined any such secondary sources that we've just discussed or described?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not, but again it is -- if you would tell me why would I discuss sources like legal immigration, birth, death, to show the ethnic composition? Q The purpose, I think, is the literature has shown, and you may disagree with me on this, but I believe the literature is quite vast in concluding quite universally that utilising these secondary sources are extremely relevant and important in order to give reliability and accuracy to the report that's being submitted when analysing these two informational sources that you did.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it would be indeed necessary to discuss these sources if I would present in my report a population projection starting with the census, 1991 census, as the base year for the projection. So using the standard demographic methods and sources like live birth, deaths, migration, I could present you with an estimate of the population by 1997, any other year, and then I would have to discuss these sources. If not, I don't think I really have to discuss these sources when I discuss -- when I was presenting population from two selected years. Already population figures were there. I didn't have to produce them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, we discussed briefly, Doctor, S228 A and B, which is an exhibit introduced by the Office of the Prosecutor yesterday, which is -- which was marked "strictly confidential" from the Ministry of Internal Affairs, Centre for the State Security Department, Banja Luka." In connection with that document, and I'm not sure if, Doctor, you have that document in front of you. If you could just advise me whether or not you do.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can have the Court, please, have the usher provide the doctor with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you, Doctor, in your professional experience, at any time have a situation where you were provided data from a source that's identified as the Ministry of Internal Affairs, Centre for the State Security Department?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the experience. This is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Any other, other than this one time?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document which is from 1995. Well, I believe there are more documents similar to this one. I might have something for 1993 like this one next to the figures from the Kozarski Vjesnik that we discussed yesterday. But I can't recall that I have more figures, statistics, produced by the State Security Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question was a little different, and I apologise if it was not clear. That is, during the years in which you became a scientist, a demographer, had you ever relied on data from an institution or institutions identified as state security departments in the Ministry of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of the Office of the Prosecutor, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, Doctor, while examining this overview, as it's captioned on page 1 of S228, did you, Doctor, make any verification as to the reliability of the data that is provided within that document? Specifically, if I may direct your attention to page 6 of the document relating to the Municipality of Prijedor which is identified under subparagraph 9.

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: 9, we have census, 1991 census. So these figures, of course, were compared with other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Doctor, whether the figures that appear on Exhibit S228A are the exact same figures as the figures that you rely on from the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slightly different, I believe. We can check this immediately with the report. The total is in my report, page 7, English translation, table 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have it. Under 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: EWA TABEAU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
